subject: Post-call: keying & logging constraints — hosting implication summary

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: keying & logging constraints — hosting implication summary

Hi Alison — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call highlights / constraints you flagged:
- Mandatory customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed key wrapping (FIPS-level controls).
- Long-term immutable logging requirement (7 years) with daily exports to customer archival store and write-once retention.
- Data residency requirement in us-east-1 for PHI-related models.
- SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM user sync and role mapping for auditability.
- Procurement target: decision window in Q1, aiming to start a POC in early Q1 if terms align.

Platform implications (high level):
- Private (VPC / on-prem) best fits the full set of asks (BYOK/HSM + in-region residency + controlled egress + long immutable logs).
- Dedicated could be feasible if we can expose the customer KMS/HSM with a validated key-wrap path and the customer is comfortable with log-export hooks to their archive.
- Hosted API (standard multi-tenant) likely ruled out due to BYOK + 7-year immutable logs, unless you accept an outsourced key escrow model and we can negotiate specific retention SLAs — not our recommendation for PHI.

Attachments sent with this message: integration-matrix-v1.xlsx (high-level mapping of features to hosting mode).

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Marcus to validate KMS/HSM integration patterns and log retention/export options — Marcus, can you share 45–60min slots next week?
2) I'll share SOC2 artifacts and a lightweight preflight checklist for Private vs Dedicated that should map to your procurement checklist.
3) If technical fit looks good, we'll scope a Private POC + an initial pricing indication for procurement.

Please let me know if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alison Ward <aw@clearwater.health>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: keying & logging constraints — hosting implication summary

Thanks, Sofia — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from security: 

- KMS/HSM: We require BYOK with keys originating from our HSM (vendor HSM or CloudHSM). Keys must be FIPS-validated, and we need deterministic key-wrap semantics (we use PKCS#11 interfaces for our on-prem HSMs).
- Key lifecycle: rotation policy managed by us; Redwood should never have access to unwrapped key material.
- Logs: Immutability requirement means write-once retention (WORM) for 7 years; we expect daily push of consolidated logs to our archival S3 bucket with server-side encryption and restricted IAM.
- SSO: Okta SAML for SSO + SCIM provisioning. We also need per-token auditability for API calls tied back to user principals.

If Marcus can confirm whether Redwood can: (a) accept customer-provided KMS endpoints and integrate with PKCS#11 or CloudHSM wrap/unwarp, and (b) provide an automated daily export of logs to our S3 with WORM policies applied, that will determine whether we pursue Private or an exceptionally configured Dedicated deployment.

I've attached a short primer on our security expectations for vendor integrations. Procurement is tracking this for a Q1 start; budget conversation will happen in December.

Best,
Alison Ward
Head of Information Security | ClearWater Health
aw@clearwater.health | +1 (617) 555-0987

Alison — thanks for the clear summary. Quick technical notes and next actions from our side.

Technical feasibility snapshot:
- KMS/HSM (BYOK): Redwood supports customer-managed keys via multiple integration patterns:
  * CloudKMS/CloudHSM: we can integrate directly with AWS KMS and CloudHSM for key wrap/unwarp using a customer-managed key policy and IAM roles.
  * PKCS#11 bridge: for on-prem HSMs we can support a PKCS#11 bridge that performs key wrapping on the customer's side — recommended approach for customers who cannot expose key endpoints into our VPC.
  * Key material: Redwood never persists unwrapped key material. Keys are stored/used only via wrapped key handles or remote KMS calls.

- Log export / retention: we can configure daily exports of consolidated access logs to a customer S3 bucket (signed uploads) and support an automated lifecycle policy on the object metadata for WORM-style retention. For true legal-only WORM we recommend configuring S3 Object Lock + Governance/Compliance mode on your side; Redwood will maintain integrity hashes and signed manifests daily.

- SSO / auditability: Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning are supported; our token layer can include per-principal audit fields and we can forward token-level metadata to your audit pipeline.

Hosting recommendation: Private VPC deployment provides the clearest path to meeting all constraints with minimal custom engineering. Dedicated is a possible compromise but will require: (a) validated CloudHSM integration and (b) an audit of network egress controls and log-forwarding endpoints.

Next actions we will take this week:
1) I'll prepare a short technical note that outlines integration patterns (PKCS#11, CloudHSM, KMS roles) — attached.
2) Neha will assemble a preflight checklist focused on security/compliance items you can use in procurement.
3) Sofia — I'll provide availability for the deep-dive slots you suggested; I can do Tue 12/1 10:00–11:00 PST.

If you can confirm the preferred deep-dive slot and provide the S3 bucket ARN + IAM principal we should use for signed uploads, we'll include concrete steps and a timeline for a Private POC.
